mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate revenues and profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 5% and CPI inflation is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong demand for housing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate continued economic strength.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between high INDPRO levels and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
